transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I get stuck doing the same checks and routines over and over until I can’t finish anything, even when I know it makes no sense. It's just incredibly exhausting, and I feel like I'm completely paralyzed by it.
Do you experience significant anxiety or distress when you're unable to complete these routines or checks, or is it more about the frustration of being stuck?

It is definitely an overwhelming dread and anxiety rather than just frustration. If I can't finish the checks, I get this awful feeling that something catastrophic is going to happen—like a house catching fire—and that it will be entirely my fault. That fear makes it absolutely impossible to just let it go.
Do you also experience unwanted, intrusive thoughts or images that are not just about the checks or routines, but perhaps about harm to yourself or others, or other disturbing themes?

Yes, my mind constantly hits me with vivid pictures of past projects failing, like a house I worked on catching fire or a deck collapsing because I missed some tiny detail. Even though those jobs passed inspection years ago, the thoughts won't stop and I end up mentally replaying every step I took instead of focusing on the present. It's like I just can't shut them out.
Do these intrusive thoughts or images of past projects failing and potential harm lead to compulsions to perform specific rituals or mental acts to try and prevent these feared outcomes?

Yes, they absolutely do. Those thoughts trigger me to check things like the stove, door locks, power tools, and tape measure numbers over and over in a very specific order. I can get stuck doing this for an hour or more because of that awful feeling that if I don't do it perfectly, a disaster will happen and it'll be my fault.

Can you tell me if these intrusive thoughts and the subsequent compulsions to check things are primarily focused on preventing specific, realistic harms, such as a fire or an accident, or if they also include more abstract or unrealistic fears?

They are definitely focused on specific, realistic disasters like a house catching fire, a deck collapsing, or someone getting hurt because I left the stove on. Even though I know checking ten times is irrational, the fears themselves are always about these concrete, terrible accidents rather than anything abstract.
Do you experience any intrusive thoughts that are unrelated to harm or danger, such as concerns about symmetry, exactness, or unwanted sexual or religious thoughts?

No, I don't really experience those kinds of thoughts about symmetry, exactness, or anything sexual or religious. My mind is pretty much entirely focused on those terrible accidents happening, like a house catching fire or a deck collapsing because I made a mistake.

Can you tell me if you have ever experienced periods where these obsessive thoughts and compulsive behaviors were absent or significantly reduced, only to return later, or have they been relatively constant since they started?

I'm not really sure, and I haven't thought about it that way. It feels like they have been pretty constant and just slowly getting worse over the last few years, rather than ever really going away and coming back.

Have you noticed any significant changes or variations in the intensity or frequency of your obsessive thoughts and compulsive behaviors over time, or in response to different situations or stressors?

Yes, they have definitely gotten much worse over time and always spike when I'm under a lot of stress. They first became really severe when I took on more responsibility at work with safety checks, and recently they got so intense during exams and planning tasks that I had to drop my construction-management course. Now, it has even spilled over into my daily life at home, making simple things like getting dinner ready or leaving the house on time a massive struggle.

Can you describe how your obsessive thoughts and compulsive behaviors affect your daily life and relationships, and are there any specific situations or events that trigger them besides the examples you've mentioned?

They've severely disrupted my life—I had to leave my foreman track and drop my construction course because I was always late, and now even making dinner or leaving the house on time causes constant frustration for my wife and family. As for other triggers, I haven't really noticed any outside of the safety checks on the stove, locks, and tools, or when I'm dealing with exams and planning tasks.
